correctness.rationale: Subtracting consecutive partial sums of the original floor recurrence gives the exact divisor formula h_c(n)=-1-c sum_{1<d<n,d|n}h_c(d), valid including n=2. With g_c=epsilon+c(u-epsilon), convolution yields h_c*g_c=epsilon+(c-1)(u-epsilon). Modulo c-1 (c>=3), g_c≡u and Möbius inversion gives h_c≡mu mod(c-1), excluding nonsquarefree composites from h=-1. On squarefree r-prime support, Boolean subset convolution gives generating function H(z)=[(c-1)e^z-(c-2)]/[c e^z-(c-1)] =1-1/c+c^{-2}e^{-z}/(1-rho e^{-z}), rho=(c-1)/c. Its rth coefficient for r>=1 is (-1)^r c^{-2} sum_{m>=1}m^r rho^{m-1}, magnitude exactly 1 at r=1 and strictly >1 at r>=2. Thus all primes exactly -1 and no composite for every fixed c>=3. Sharp boundary c=0 at n4, c=1 at n30 via mu, c=2 at n8 by prime-power formula. Independently evaluated ORIGINAL floor recurrence versus the divisor recurrence for c=0..8, n<=180, all prime/composite classifications within cutoff; this bounded computation corroborates but does not replace the infinite argument.
